items.original_text: Filing step: Identify and enter into escrow for an ABC Type 42 (or Type 41 upgradable to Type 42) license currently held by a bar located inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. What to say: Engage an ABC license broker to search for available Type 42 or Type 41 licenses held by bars within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD boundaries (roughly Mission Street from 15th to Cesar Chavez, extending west). Verify with the broker and Planning that the source premises is inside the SUD. Negotiate the purchase price and enter escrow; make the lease at 995 Valencia contingent on ABC approval of the license transfer. Budget $25,000–$75,000 for a Type 42 in San Francisco (prices vary widely). Do not file the CUA until you have a license in escrow or a commitment letter, because Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C) makes the license source a hard requirement.

items.original_text: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $7,153 to $24,050. Notes: Timeline: 120–300 days is the time to obtain the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per catalog entry, filing to Commission approval), Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days, filing to Commission approval), Health permit to operate (14–45 days, application to final inspection and issuance), and Building permit with change of use (14–120 days for plan review, plus construction time). These are run in sequence (CUA first, then POE and building permit in parallel after CUA approval, then health permit after building final), so the total timeline is dominated by the CUA. The 120–300 day range is for approvals; it does not include time to denials, withdrawals or cancellations. Two comparable bar CUAs in the immediate area (2010.0680C and 2019-014253CUA) were withdrawn or cancelled before a Commission vote, one after 155 days and one after 98 days, so those figures are not included in this approval timeline. Cost: $7,153–$24,050 covers CUA filing fee ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost and fee waiver eligibility), POE permit application ($2,708), health permit to operate ($470) and health plan check ($828–$2,500), building permit ($800–$15,000), and sign permit ($300–$1,500). ABC license transfer fees ($1,000–$1,600) and the purchase price of the license itself ($25,000–$75,000 estimated for a Type 42 in SF) are not government fees and are excluded. State and city business registration, tax accounts and staff training total roughly $250–$1,000 and are also excluded as non-entitlement costs. Music licenses (ASCAP, BMI) are annual subscription fees, not one-time government costs. The timeline assumes no appeals, no discretionary review, and a complete application; protests or incomplete plans can add 60–180 days.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $7,153 to $24,050. Notes: Timeline: 120–300 days is the time to obtain the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per catalog entry, filing to Commission approval), Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days, filing to Commission approval), Health permit to operate (14–45 days, application to final inspection and issuance), and Building permit with change of use (14–120 days for plan review, plus construction time). These are run in sequence (CUA first, then POE and building permit in parallel after CUA approval, then health permit after building final), so the total timeline is dominated by the CUA. The 120–300 day range is for approvals; it does not include time to denials, withdrawals or cancellations. Two comparable bar CUAs in the immediate area (2010.0680C and 2019-014253CUA) were withdrawn or cancelled before a Commission vote, one after 155 days and one after 98 days, so those figures are not included in this approval timeline. Cost: $7,153–$24,050 covers CUA filing fee ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost and fee waiver eligibility), POE permit application ($2,708), health permit to operate ($470) and health plan check ($828–$2,500), building permit ($800–$15,000), and sign permit ($300–$1,500). ABC license transfer fees ($1,000–$1,600) and the purchase price of the license itself ($25,000–$75,000 estimated for a Type 42 in SF) are not government fees and are excluded. State and city business registration, tax accounts and staff training total roughly $250–$1,000 and are also excluded as non-entitlement costs. Music licenses (ASCAP, BMI) are annual subscription fees, not one-time government costs. The timeline assumes no appeals, no discretionary review, and a complete application; protests or incomplete plans can add 60–180 days.
